# Born In Betrayal

*Pages PDF 69-75*

## **Valerion’s Blackswords**
## **Born in Betrayal**
The Blackswords are a mercenary company, fighting for pay and prisoners across the world. They appear to humans as plain-dressed elves from distant lands, carefully concealing their identity. Given their professional prowess in battle, most patrons overlook their cruelty in combat and demands to take captives away with them. 

Taking his remaining retainers, Valerion fled along the coast until he reached the relative safety of Clar Karond. There on the docks, he signed himself and his men on as mercenaries for _Temple of Spite_ , receiving refuge in return for obedience. Setting sail on a ravenship bound for the ark, he swore never to return to Naggaroth until he had accumulated enough fame and power to take revenge on House Morandor. 

## **Goals**
The Blackswords were once the household guard of House Temendros of Hag Graef, whose dreadlords held exalted positions in the city’s ruling elite. Some even thought the head of the house would one day replace the drachau, and such ambition was their undoing. 

On Death Night, 2290 IC, House Temendros was betrayed by their vassals in House Morandor. As night fell over Hag Graef, prowling witch elves poured into Temendros’ tower through an unlocked door and murdered every living being within in orgiastic worship to Khaine. 

Not all Temendros were present that night. The heir, Valerion Temendros, was with a detachment of household troops sent to punish a reaving clan of shades that were ravaging their rural estates. When word reached him of the perfidy of House Morandor, he knew that flight was his only hope for survival. 

**Wealth, reputation and an exciting life.** For many dark elf mercenaries lust for wealth goes beyond gold, as captives are also valuable. Proving their skill in battle brings status for the Blackswords and deters others from trying to dominate them. 

**Protect Durith Helbane.** The Blackswords gained much from the failed mutiny. They elevated their position in the ark’s hierarchy by persecuting those labelled traitors on behalf of the fleetmaster. This was a calculated move by Valerion and Damina Hroska to raise the Blackswords about other soldiers in the warhost and buy independence from the chain of command. 

**Revenge against House Morandor.** Valerion Temendros wants revenge on those who destroyed his house. The need to wreak terrible retribution consumes his soul. Unlike most Druchii, his patience lasts decades. He bides his time, building his experience, power, and wealth, until he can one day return to Hag Graef and cleanse his ancestral home with Morandor blood. 

## **Rivals and Allies**
On _Temple of Spite_ , the Blackswords’ principal alliance is with the fleetmaster, by whose grace they serve and live. Valerion has tied his fortunes to Helbane’s, and without his patronage, the last Temendros might have fallen beneath the blades of House Morandor’s assassins. Valerion shares the spoils of the Blackswords’ adventures with Helbane and his mercenaries act as Helbane’s enforcers on the ark, having taken his side in the attempted mutiny and leading the subsequent purge. 

Though Damina is sworn to protect her captain, the death hag’s poisoned words gradually erode away at the seriousness with which she holds to her oath. 

Hermizor of Arguental possesses the boundless ego of the mediocre. He has nowhere near his captain’s talent, yet he schemes to make the company ‘Hermizor’s Blackswords’ by quietly encouraging the warriors’ discontent. 

## **Meeting the Blackswords**
The Blackswords have a profitable working relationship with Captain Flariel and the crew of _The Raptor’s Talon_ , so when the _Talon_ strikes, the Blackswords sometimes accompany Flariel’s corsairs on raids. Valerion’s mercenaries support Flariel against his rival captains, a favour the reaver returns with spoils and opportunities for mercenary work. 

The Blackswords do not consider themselves subservient to Lord Tualarc’s warhost, though they fight alongside them. The commander hopes to bring them to heel, but Helbane’s patronage makes this tricky, if he can diminish them in the fleetmaster’s estimation, he might succeed. 

Unknown to Valerion, his chief enemy on _Temple of Spite_ is Death Hag Kheitalla, the most powerful Khainite on board. Originally an acolyte at the temple of Khaine in Hag Graef, on joining the ark she was shocked to discover a living Temendros, as she had been among the witch elves who slaughtered his kin, and was shamed to find a survivor. Unable to move against Valerion directly, she foments hatred and resentment among his men. Her principal target is Damina Hroska, whom she hopes will one day honour Khaine by bringing her the captain’s heart. 

## **Internal Tensions**
To their paymasters and other dark elves, the Blackswords appear unified, professional, and ruthlessly efficient. Behind this façade, there is disquiet in the ranks. 

Among the warriors, there is growing resentment toward Valerion because he increasingly claims a greater share of the pay and captives. Complaints are met by a menacing glare or even the edge of his sword, but some warriors have begun to wonder whether it is time for a new captain. 

Valerion, always taciturn, confides in his lieutenants less than before, leading to tension among the officers. Not only do they feel slighted, but they fear their captain might be about to replace or even betray them. This feeds Damina Hroska’s doubts, once buried, about her decision to leave the temple of Khaine. Kheitalla has sensed this and approached Damina quietly, secretly, encouraging her to repent before Valerion turns on her. 

There are several reasons an encounter with Valerion’s Blackswords might involve something other than violence. While immensely cruel by Old World standards, Valerion is no fool. He can see when his interests are best served by temporary cooperation, rather than by splitting skulls. If faced with a powerful mutual enemy — such as greenskins or Chaos marauders, the Blackswords will make a pragmatic alliance with the Characters. If they are employed by a human paymaster, the Characters could fight alongside them as mercenaries themselves or on behalf of their patron. The Characters may even be sent to hire them. 

Cooperation is not without risk and the Blackswords keep their end of a bargain only so long as it meets their interests, so the Characters better hope they judged those interests correctly. 

## **Disposition**
Valerion’s command usually comprises around 130 Druchii, though numbers vary due to casualties. They are rarely encountered in full, with different units deployed on the ark while other venture forth on land. 

- **Captain Valerion Temendros** leads 24 Swordsmen, hand-picked for loyalty and obedience. The standard bearer, Aenselir Starkblood, is a survivor from Hag Graef. 

- **Hermizor of Arguental** commands ‘The Fellstalkers’, 24 Swordsmen with a reputation for showy swordwork. 

- **Seethian The Grim** leads the ‘Twilight Wraiths’, 20 Swordsmen known to file their teeth into points. 

- **‘The Oathblooded’** are the remaining regiment of 30 Swordsmen under the iron command of Ghalil Makhar. She is charged with looking for potential traitors or spies amongst new recruits to the Blackswords. 

- **Zelendial Serekhar** leads the Blackswords’ Darkshards, the ‘Ashen Bolts’, comprising 28 Dark Elves with repeater crossbows. As they do not fight face-to-face with the enemy, they receive a smaller share of the pay than the Swordsmen. This damages their morale, and they are currently the most disgruntled mercenaries in the group. 

- **Damina Hroska** joins no regiment, going wherever best suits the Blackswords’ needs on the battlefield. 

Some Blackswords are on duty aboard the Temple of Spite at any given time, while others are away on various raiding expeditions or mercenary work. The Twilight Wraiths are better suited to duties on the ark, given their dental adornment. 

## **Appearance**
The Blackswords’ armour consists of a blackened chain coat and black open helm. Bleakswords carry a tall shield and slender sword meant to slip past an opponent’s guard, while darkshards carry repeating crossbows. 

Banners and shields show the Elthárin rune meaning ‘mastery’ beneath crossed swords, on an unadorned black field — suitably neutral heraldry to obscure their true origins. Some of the regiment’s warriors depict the rune urithair, meaning destruction, conquest, sacrifice of the innocent, but disguised or flipped in memory of the destruction of House Temendros. 

## **Mutual Interests — Easy Encounter**
Somewhere on the edges of the Empire, the Characters have traced an ancient book to the ruins of a castle held by an outlaw chief. They even have a map showing a forgotten escape tunnel leading from a fireplace in the master bedroom to a sluice gate by the moat. It should be a simple matter, they need to sneak in, get the book, and get out. 

When they arrive, the Characters discover that the castle is under siege by Valerion’s Blackswords. The burghers of a nearby town are sick of the bandits’ depredations, so they hired the best mercenaries to solve the problem permanently. 

The castle has proven more formidable than expected and, lacking siege equipment, Valerion faces the prospect of a long siege, which does not suit the Blackswords. Now the Characters are faced with sneaking through a camp of bored elves (whom they likely do not recognise as Druchii), as well as dealing with the desperate bandits. 

Should the Characters contact the elves, they find Valerion open to a deal. He will let them pass through his lines to recover their book, but in return they must open the gates to his troops. Matters become complicated if the outlaw chief discovers them and offers them another deal: the book in return for his escape. 

## **Stiff Competition — Medium Encounter**
The Characters are in a city where the local ruler is hiring mercenaries to defend his lands. He hopes to recruit a unit of elves who are charging an exorbitant fee. Their lead negotiator is an elf woman, Damina Hroska and while she has the Count wrapped around her little finger, he needs proof these mercenaries are worth the gold 

The Count offers payment to anyone willing to prove in a practice bout that they can outshine the Blackswords’ prowess in both close and ranged combat, and so drive down the price. Damina’s Druchii arrogance overcomes any qualms and she gladly takes up the offer, asking only that she can select two prisoners should the Characters lose. 

During the competition, the Characters may notice incongruities about these ‘Caledorian’ elves. In mock combat, the Blackswords are exceptionally brutal and seem to have trouble restraining themselves. There are accidents with equipment — the Characters’ bows and guns fail inexplicably. Is this an act of sabotage? If the Party can prove the elves have been cheating, then the Count, an honorable man, will refuse the Damina’s price, thus earning the Characters her personal enmity. 

## **Rescue Mission — Hard Encounter**
Raiders in black ships have struck the Empire’s coast, and the Blackswords were among them. Among the captives was a Shallyan holy woman, a hermit reputed to have powers of healing beyond those of a priestess. News is spreading rapidly and regional rulers fear unrest by people afraid of the goddess’s displeasure. The Characters are dispatched to rescue the holy woman and, if possible, anyone else taken. 

Though the reavers have a day’s start on them, it will take them three days to reach Kirkjugarður Langskipa in Norsca, where they plan to exchange some of the captives for fresh water and provisions. The Characters have a choice — they can try to intercept the ship at sea, but this means combat over the open ocean against Captain Frosthand’s corsairs and the Blackswords. There is no guarantee of rescuing the prisoners alive, or of escaping with their own lives. 

They could try to secure the captives in Kirkjugarður Langskipa — exchanging goods with the Blackswords, using violence, or coming to an arrangement with the local Norscans. 

## **Captain Valerion Temendros, ‘the Flayer’**
Last scion of a massacred noble line, Valerion Temendros has been the captain of Valerion’s Blackswords for over 200 years. Since abasing himself and his remaining warriors before Duriath Helbane in return for protection, he has come to serve the lord of _Temple of Spite_ as both sword and shield — a sword that strikes fast and slices without mercy, and a shield against all enemies, especially those aboard the black ark.

## **Armour**
Rejecting the devotion to style so common among Druchii, Valerion focuses obsessively on his goals, both immediate and long-term. Anything that does not serve those goals is a distraction and a weakness to be cut out. Tall and strongly built for a dark elf, he wears his hair cut short, clearly exposing the left ear that was once cropped by a sword cut. His clothing is plain and practical, and his weapons and armour unadorned. 

Though he does not share their sense of fashion and style, Valerion Temendros is a Druchii, and still capable of unspeakable cruelty. He earned the nickname ‘the Flayer’ in Kislev, when he ordered his troops to peel the skins from the citizens of an entire town in revenge for them failing to inform him of an enemy ambush. For Valerion, this was business, not pleasure, ‘to discourage others’.

**Night Vision:** See clearly for 20 yards and extend the illumination distance of light sources by 20 yards. 

**Combat Aware:** Take a **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test to ignore the _Surprised_ Condition from an ambush. **Combat Reflexes:** Combat Initiative counts as 80. **Inspiring:** Can influence 5 times the normal number of followers with Leadership Skill during battle. 

**Menacing:** Reverse dice of failed Intimidate Test, if so, the maximum result is 1 SL. 

**Read/Write:** Can read and write. 

**Shieldsman:** When carrying a shield, once per Round, you may lose Advantage to either grant your shield’s AP bonus to an adjacent ally who is not carrying a shield of their own, or, upon winning any Opposed Melee Test (as either attacker or defender), push your opponent 2 yards directly back from yourself and no longer count as Engaged. 

**Warleader:** Allies influenced with _Leadership_ during battle may use the character’s _Leadership_ rather than their _Cool_ to resist _Fear_ until the end of the battle.

## **Damina Hroska, Assassin of Khaine and Business Manager**
Damina Hroska looks young and waiflike, which belies her 350 years. She is the presentable face of Valerion’s Blackswords, handling all negotiations for the warband, as Valerion himself has no patience for the fripperies of diplomacy. Dressed in fine silks of blood red, black, and indigo, she is charming and flirtatious in dealmaking, using her words and actions skillfully from behind an ornate Cathayan fan, the same fan she can use to slit a man’s throat with one slash.

The dangers of temple politics eventually led her to _Temple of Spite_ , where she found a role with the Blackswords, first as an assassin, then as Valerion’s ‘mouth’, a role she took to as easily as that of professional murderer. 

When in the field, Damina exchanges her silks for armour and her fan for blades, to blend in with the troops. She aims to wreak havoc by assassinating the opponents’ leaders, either in the heat of battle or in the quiet of the enemy camp. The Blackswords have won several battles and sieges when their adversaries woke up one morning to find their leaders’ heads resting on their chests.

## **Hermizor of House Arguental, Scheming Second-In-Command**
While Valerion Temendros scorns Druchii fashion and fads, his second-in-command, Hermizor Carveheart, embraces them as a reason to live. A younger son of the noble House Arguental of Clar Karond, Hermizor was sent abroad to gain experience and glory for his family, and was assigned to the Blackswords in a deal between the city’s dreadlords and Duriath Helbane. To say he was imposed would be an understatement, as would saying Hermizor and Valerion dislike each other. 

A young adult Druchii, Hermizor cuts a dashing, noble figure. His skin is flawless, testifying to his lack of experience. His black armour is etched in gold with images of daemons, while his weapons are bejewelled. His leather cloak is made from the flesh of an Asur dyed black and lined with blood red silk. Hermizor is never angrier than when Valerion makes him exchange his finery for plain clothes and armour to appear as a nondescript elf. 

For all his foppishness, Hermizor is a Druchii through and through. Cruel as any, but not nearly as smart as he believes, he plots to eliminate Valerion, perhaps even offer him as a sacrifice to his true master, Slaanesh.

## **On the Black Ark**
_Temple of Spite_ serves several purposes for the Blackswords and, in comparison to Naggaroth, it is a place of refuge. Here, under Duriath Helbane’s patronage and protection, Valerion has time to train his men and plot his strategy. The ark is far from safe, but the occasional conflict with other inhabitants pales in comparison to the dangers awaiting them in Naggaroth. 

_Temple of Spite_ is Valerion’s path to his ultimate goal, as its countless raids around the world facilitate his quest to accumulate power. On each voyage, he has a clear goal, as simple as fame, gold, and prisoners, or as arcane as a magical device rumoured to lie within the Lustrian jungle. Mercenary work is the means to an end, and the ark is the vehicle to get there. The key is to keep Duriath Helbane satisfied and his rivals afraid. 

## **In the Old World**
Why do Valerion’s Blackswords spend so much time in the Old World when there is an entire world to plunder? The constant wars are a steady source of income, and their squabbles do not pose the dangers of Lustrian jungles or the northern wastes. There is prestige for a human general to field a regiment of elves in their army, and intimidation plays a role, too. More than once a rebellious militia or mercenary force has quit the field when they learned they faced the Blackswords, so the Old World’s nobles and wealthy burghers pay dearly for such feared fighters. 

The Old World’s wars also provide valuable training for Valerion’s troops. Formal battles and sieges hone the Blacksword’s skills, while fighting against rebel irregulars in the hills of Tilea or Norsca teach them what it is like to be surrounded by enemies. There is a twin goal: to keep the unit fit for the next war against Ulthuan, and for the eventual return to Hag Graef. 

## **The Blackswords in Lustria**
The Blackswords have served Helbane around the globe. In recent decades, their focus beyond the Old World is Lustria, where Duriath Helbane is considering an alliance with Luthor Harkon, Master of the Vampire Coast and self-proclaimed Emperor of Lustria. To please Malerion and Anethra Helbane, and reap glory for himself, Helbane seeks to seize a magical artefact hidden in the lizardman city of Tlax, a mysterious item known as the Impossible Prism. 

## **Among the Vampires**
For the past century, the Blackswords have regularly visited the Vampire Coast. Sometimes it is only for a season or two, but on other occasions, they have passed several years there. Unable to disembark in Naggaroth, the Blackswords treat their visits to the Vampire Coast and its lone city, New Bechafen, as a form of shore leave, mixing business with relaxation. 

There is no need to hide their true nature, so they can revel in those entertainments that give a Druchii the most pleasure, tormenting those weaker than them. 

Visits to Lustria are not just for sport, however. When hired by Harkon or one of his underlings, the Blackswords play an important role in securing and expanding the vampire’s dark realm, and have gained valuable experience fighting in the continent’s jungles and grasslands. Sometimes they form a mobile strike force as part of a larger army of zombies and human subjects, the dark elves’ skill and savagery devastating the surprised lizardman armies. 

This is just a means to a larger goal: proving to Luthor Harkon that an alliance with _Temple of Spite_ would serve both their interests. When calling at New Bechafen, Captain Valerion negotiates with Harkon, though the dark elf finds it frustrating, as the vampire lord’s demands are often irrational and his personality changes come without warning. 

On one visit, Valerion found he could no longer tolerate Harkon’s eccentricity, but neither could he fail Helbane. He gave the matter over to Damina Hroska, who soon realised what her captain had missed. She saw that not only was Harkon mad, but there were multiple personas living within him, at least two of which, little Wihelmina and scholarly Sancho, she could establish a rapport with. Negotiations have gone more smoothly since, though the dominant Harkon persona still refuses to support the Blackswords in an assault on Tlax. 

Recently, new possibilities have arisen when, in carefully phrased messages and subtle hints, Harkon’s ghoul chancellor, Black Jens, made it known that he seeks his own alliance with the Blackswords, though on different terms. In return for an alliance against Tlax, he wants Valerion’s aid to seize the throne in a coup against Harkon. It is a proposal Captain Valerion finds increasingly attractive. 

## **Fancy Meeting You Here**
A campaign set in Lustria could include encounters with Valerion’s Blackswords, working with Luthor Harkon or for their own interests to find the Impossible Prism. Should there be a high or wood elf among the Characters, then a clash is almost inevitable. Otherwise, it is not unthinkable that the Characters and the Blackswords could work together to explore Tlax, the latter masquerading as sea elves. They could deal with the Blackswords in one of the port towns of the Lustrian coast, as they plan an expedition to the interior or offer to accompany a wealthy Imperial explorer. Should the Characters reach an accord with the lizardmen, they could be drawn into defending an ancient site such as Tlax from the Blackswords.
